rationale.complete: Round 1 done: card and dated predictions before data; synthetic validation on real call grids (4 units x 5 worlds x 10 reps) with a dated pre-data amendment (hour blocks); replication on 66 units / 35 periods with variants (trim, exogenous, decision-time, heterogeneous radius, quiet recipients), shift null and comparison with H25/H42/H50; 3 natives with dated predictions; confirm.py frozen, guarded and dry-run. Missing: holdout run, regime-I clock, multi-hop correction.
rationale.faithfulness: The read-out linear-response model is identified (synthetic bias <= 3%, null size 7.5-10%) and makes unfitted predictions that pass (subcritical, address gating x19, per-read dilution with N, rank agreement with H42 rho 0.55). The HH's own signature (lagged > equal-time) fails, the unnamed part is at the placebo's resolution, and H50's estimator disagrees by a factor 2. Scorecard A1 B1 C1 D1 E1 F2 G1 H1 I0.
rationale.usefulness: A calibrated, field-free loop-gain gauge computable from call logs, with a clear operator message: the equal-time dial overstates coupling, naming carries it, and the village is far from talk runaway at any size seen. A monitor, not a lever.

one_line: Read-out talk coupling is subcritical (g_lag ~0.13 in regime III, ~0 elsewhere), carried by named messages; the equal-time dial overstates it (lagged > equal-time in only 7/35 periods).

models.note: Mean-field loop gain on the call clock; subcritical, not above equal-time
